Bug_Details:
The hasNext() method invokes the next() method. This is almost certainly wrong,
since the hasNext() method is not supposed to change the state of the iterator,
and the next method is supposed to change the state of the iterator.
Bug_Explanation: The bug here is a violation of the Iterator interface contract. The hasNext() method is supposed to check if there is a next element without advancing the iteration. The next() method should be called only after hasNext() returns true. In this case, the hasNext() method is directly followed by a call to next(), which is not compliant with the Iterator interface contract.
Trigger_Explanation: Test fails because the hasNext() method directly calls the next() method without checking if there is a next element. The next() method should only be called after hasNext() has confirmed there is a next element.
